newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Benign G7 summit dampens dollar vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Benign G7 summit dampens dollar vols.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/yen options slipped as the G7 summit meeting over the weekend yielded little to agitate the spot currency market.

Many who had expected the G7 to make a strong statement on the US-Japan trade gap had bought up dollar vols last week, and were now selling off as the G7 had remained fairly benign on the issue and bolstered spot dollar/yen, traders said.

"The G7 turned out to be a bit of a non-event...and everyone who bought volatilities going into the G7 are now trying to get rid of their long positions," said James Binney, fund manager at GNI in London.
"Dollar/yen vols, which have been of most interest recently, have moved very much in line with the spot market. When dollar/yen goes up, vols come right off," Binney said.
Spot dollar/yen was at 115.42/47 at 1135 GMT in the aftermath of the G7, up nearly one yen from its late Friday European level.
One-month dollar/yen vols had slid to 10.00/10.40 percent from Friday's 10.70/11.00.

Demand for yen calls, which shot up last week on expectations that the G7 meeting would highlight US-Japan trade friction, eased somewhat. One-month 25-delta risk reversals were at 1.7/2.1 with a bias for yen calls, against 2.1/2.4 on Friday.

At the summit, U.S. President Bill Clinton warned that a continued rise in Japan's trade surplus with the U.S. could lead to economic war between the two nations. Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, for his part, said the recent rise in the surplus was due to temporary factors and that it would not last.
Dollar/mark vols were steady after the spot rate firmed slightly in the wake of the G7 meeting, with one-month vols at 8.30/8.60 percent against 8.40/8.70 on Friday.
The risk reversal was biased towards mark puts at 0.1/0.2 against Friday's 0.0/0.3.

Meanwhile, mark/lira vols dwindled as the spot rate dropped to four-month lows on Monday. Spot mark/lira crept back up to 978.60/90 after hitting a low of 976.60 earlier, compared with 977.60/90 in late trade on Friday.
One-month vols on the pair were at 3.15/3.65 percent against Friday's 3.20/3.70.
"It's very, very inexpensive for something that's as volatile as the mark/lira," said David Donora, head of forex options at CIBC in London.

"The market perceives that 975 to 980 (lire to the mark) is a range of stability, and it perceives that 985 to 995 is a range of higher volatility, so anytime we're down here, the market likes to sell the vol," he said.
